title: Gusle (one-string fiddle)
summary: The gusle is a one-string fiddle of the western Balkans. A deep pear-shaped body of carved maple is covered with a goatskin and topped by a carved ram’s head. The player holds it upright between the knees, bows the single horsehair string and sings the long story-songs of the region over the steady drone.
howToPlay: One long string runs down the neck. Each lane marks a place to stop the string, the lowest note at the top.
A bead slides down to the spot. Press and bow as it lands.
The line is short and steady, with the voice of the story carried by the notes.
Learn the phrase by echo, then play it through with the pulse.
rules: The string is stopped at eight places, giving a scale with a flat third and flat seventh.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Songs count ten slow pulses to a line.
heritageNote: The gusle accompanies long story-songs of the western Balkans. The single string and the carved ram’s head are its signature, and the player keeps a steady drone while the melody rises and falls by a few notes.
